postgresql-workbench.sqlAuthoring.aliasS.description: Alias strategy used when PostgreSQL Workbench composes a query from dragged relations. Changes apply to the next composition.

postgresql-workbench.sqlAuthoring.syntax.description: Maximum PostgreSQL syntax-tree depth used to classify SQL safely before execution and composition. Code Moniker applies this client-selected budget without an additional server cap.
Maximum PostgreSQL syntax-tree nodes used to classify SQL safely before execution and composition. Increase this client-selected budget for exceptionally large SQL documents.

postgresql-workbench.sql.statementTimeou.description: Default PostgreSQL Statement timeout in milliseconds for SQL Scratchpads and free SQL documents. Each Scratchpad can persist its own override.

postgresql-workbench.workbench.schemaSyn.description: Opt in to automatic PostgreSQL schema synchronization for Connections without an explicit override. Provisioning remains a separate confirmed action. Data changes (DML) never trigger synchronization.

postgresql-workbench.workbench.schemaSyn.patternErrorMessage: Use a lower-case, unquoted PostgreSQL identifier of at most 63 characters; pg_ prefixes are reserved.
postgresql-workbench.workbench.schemaSyn.description: PostgreSQL schema containing the Workbench DDL notification functions. Event triggers remain database-level objects and are not contained by this schema.

postgresql-workbench.workbench.codeMonik.description: Maximum duration in milliseconds for a Code Moniker daemon command or workspace readiness transition used by Workbench indexing, navigation, graph queries, and debugger syntax analysis. Changes apply to the next extension session.

postgresql-workbench.workbench.graph.com.description: Zoom level below which PostgreSQL graph nodes switch from detailed cards to compact named cards. Changes apply immediately to an open graph.
Font scale used for object names in compact PostgreSQL graph nodes. Changes apply immediately to an open graph.

postgresql-workbench.workbench.graph.edg.description: Font scale applied to PostgreSQL graph edge labels. Changes apply immediately to an open graph.

postgresql-workbench.results.maxRows.description: Maximum number of PostgreSQL rows retained for SQL selections and debug results. It is also used as the Scratchpad page size when results.pageSize has not been configured explicitly.

postgresql-workbench.results.pageSize.description: Number of rows requested by each LIMIT/OFFSET result page.

postgresql-workbench.results.maxCellByte.description: Hard maximum number of UTF-8 bytes retained for one result cell. Grid display remains compact; inspection and export use the retained value.

postgresql-workbench.results.nonPagedMax.description: Maximum rows retained for Scratchpad statements that cannot be paged safely, including data-modifying statements with RETURNING.

postgresql-workbench.results.autoReveal.description: Automatically reveal the PostgreSQL Results panel without taking keyboard focus when a debugged SQL call completes or fails.

postgresql-workbench.dataView.hideKeyCol.markdownDescription: Open a Data View with its identity and relationship columns hidden. They stay projected, so rows remain identified and editable, and the Columns menu offers them back at any time.

postgresql-workbench.tests.patterns.description: Glob patterns used to discover pgTAP test functions, matched against schema.function. Matching functions must return SETOF text; zero-argument functions can be run automatically. Schemas containing matched tests are treated as test infrastructure for coverage mapping.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.include.description: Glob patterns for routines eligible for coverage, matched against schema.name(identity arguments). An empty list includes all discovered routines.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.exclude.description: Glob patterns for routines excluded from coverage, matched after the include patterns.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.maxRoutine.description: Maximum number of PL/pgSQL routines instrumented by one coverage request.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.maxOutputL.description: Maximum number of TAP output lines attached to each VS Code test result.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.maxOutputB.description: Maximum TAP payload retained for one pgTAP test. Individual rows are truncated in PostgreSQL before transmission.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.maxParalle.description: Maximum number of independent PostgreSQL databases covered in parallel.

postgresql-workbench.coverage.timeoutMs.description: Maximum duration in milliseconds for one database coverage suite, including rollback and cleanup.

connection.description: Connection ID from the PL/pgSQL connection manager (e.g. 'localhost:5432/mydb:postgres'). If omitted, uses the active Connection.

sql.description: SQL statement to debug (CALL or SELECT). Optional when 'routine' is provided.

routine.description: Structured routine target used by the extension to launch debug sessions without interpolating SQL arguments.

routineArgs.description: Structured argument values bound by the debug adapter.

stopOnEntry.description: Stop at the first line of the function (default: true)

resultMaxRows.description: Maximum number of target SQL result rows retained for display.

walkthroughs.title: Getting Started with PostgreSQL Workbench
walkthroughs.description: Set up PostgreSQL debugging, SQL authoring, and pgTAP coverage in 7 steps.

steps.title: Start a Local Database or Add a PostgreSQL Connection
steps.description:
For the fastest setup, let the extension pull a ready-to-debug PostgreSQL image, start it locally, and connect it automatically.

[Start with Docker](command:postgresql-workbench.startDockerDebugDatabase)

Already have PostgreSQL running? [Add Connection](command:postgresql-workbench.addConnection)

steps.title: Verify Connection & pldbgapi
steps.description:
Once connected, the status bar shows the Connection name and the sidebar shows your functions. If pldbgapi is missing, the extension offers to install it.

Prerequisites:
```
# postgresql.conf
shared_preload_libraries = 'plugin_debugger'
```
```sql
CREATE EXTENSION pldbgapi;
```

steps.title: Browse Functions
steps.description:
Open PostgreSQL Workbench to browse every connected database index and SQL Scratchpads in separate, resizable views.

[Open Workbench](command:postgresql-workbench-connections.focus)

steps.title: Author SQL from Sources
steps.description:
Open a `.sql` file or a Scratchpad cell and pick its connection once. Every non-empty PostgreSQL Statement gets a **Run SQL** CodeLens, **Format Document** uppercases keywords and indents with two spaces, and completion suggests indexed schemas, tables, views, columns, functions, and procedures.

Drag one object from **Schemas** into a SQL editor or Scratchpad to compose SQL: a `SELECT` for a table or view, a `JOIN` when a foreign key connects it to the query under the cursor, a call for a function or procedure, or a DML harness for a trigger. Drop into a Data View to extend its query, or into the Cockpit to focus the graph. Composed SQL is never executed automatically.

[Open a SQL File](command:workbench.action.files.openFile)

steps.title: Set a Breakpoint
steps.description: Click in the gutter next to a PL/pgSQL line to set a breakpoint. Only executable lines (assignments, IF, LOOP, RETURN, etc.) can have breakpoints — non-steppable lines are rejected automatically.

steps.title: Launch a Debug Session
steps.description:
Three ways to start debugging:
- **CodeLens**: Click "Debug" above a `CREATE FUNCTION`, `CALL`, or `SELECT` statement
- **Sidebar**: Right-click a function → Debug
- **launch.json**: Add a `postgresql-workbench` configuration

[Open a SQL File](command:workbench.action.files.openFile)

steps.title: Run pgTAP Tests with Coverage
steps.description:
Install `pgtap` in your development database and define zero-argument `SETOF text` test functions. The default discovery patterns are `*_ut.test_*` and `*_it.test_*`, configurable globally or per workspace.

Coverage is transactional and independent from pldebugger.

[Open Testing](command:workbench.view.testing.focus)

scripts.pretest: npm run build && tsc -p . --outDir dist && node ../scripts/test/mark-esm.mjs && node ../scripts/test/build-vscode-smoke.mjs

scripts.test:acceptance: npm run test:acceptance:prepare && playwright test --config tests/acceptance/playwright/acceptance.config.ts && playwright test --config tests/acceptance/playwright/index-lifecycle.config.ts && playwright test --config tests/acceptance/playwright/schema-sync.config.ts
scripts.test:acceptance:graph-dnd: npm run build:production && npm run test:acceptance:typecheck && playwright test --config tests/acceptance/playwright/acceptance.config.ts tests/acceptance/specs/acceptance.spec.ts --grep 'Workbench graph'
